original_value: The m-polar fuzzy sets (mF sets) have a representative and fundamental role in several fields of science and decision-making. The fusion of mF sets with several other theories of mathematics has become a favorable practice for depicting numerous types of uncertainties under multi-polar information. In this article, we introduce an innovative hybrid model, called m-polar hesitant fuzzy sets (mHF-sets), a hybridization of hesitancy and mF sets, which enables us to tackle multi-polar information with hesitancy. Hesitancy incorporates symmetry into the treatment of the data, whereas the m-polar fuzzy format allows for differentiated or asymmetric sources of information. We highlight and explore basic key properties of mHF-sets and formulate intrinsic operations. Moreover, we develop an m-polar hesitant fuzzy TOPSIS (mHF-TOPSIS) approach for multi-criteria group decision-making (MCGDM), which is a natural extension of the TOPSIS method to this framework. We describe applications of mHF-sets in group decision-making. Further, we show the efficiency of our proposed approach by applying it to the industrial field. Finally, we generate a computer programming code that implements our decision-making procedure for ease of lengthy calculations.

result.paraphrase: m-polar fuzzy sets (mF sets) play a central and foundational role in many areas of science and decision-making. Their combination with various other mathematical theories has become a useful way to represent many kinds of uncertainty in multi-polar information. In this paper, we present a new hybrid model, m-polar hesitant fuzzy sets (mHF-sets), formed by combining hesitancy with mF sets, allowing multi-polar information to be handled with hesitancy. Hesitancy adds symmetry to data treatment, while the m-polar fuzzy structure supports differentiated or asymmetric information sources. We discuss the main basic properties of mHF-sets and define intrinsic operations. In addition, we develop an m-polar hesitant fuzzy TOPSIS (mHF-TOPSIS) method for multi-criteria group decision-making (MCGDM), extending TOPSIS naturally to this setting. We outline applications of mHF-sets in group decision-making. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach through an industrial application. Finally, we provide computer code that implements the decision-making procedure to simplify lengthy calculations.
